transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Silva (Redwood CSM); Elena Ruiz (Lead ML Eng, Mistral Harbor), Tom Briggs (CTO), Sanjay Mehta (Infra), Ava Li (Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review token economics (tokens/sec/$), caching savings from prefix/KV caching, and batching tradeoffs. Customer ran two replays since last week: one short-head heavy (lots of short prompts) and one long-context validation run. Focus: reduce p95 tail latency while preserving tokens-per-dollar.

Topics covered:
- Token throughput per dollar comparisons across models and quant profiles
- Observed savings from prefix cache (approx numbers discussed)
- Continuous batching vs static batch sizes and effects on tail latency
- Dedicated vs hosted route for pilot if Mistral needs guaranteed throughput
- Security checklist questions (SOC2, KMS for keys, VPC peering)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Elena: Elena here. Tom here. Sanjay on infra. Ava on product.
[00:10] Ravi: ravi from redwood. i'll kick off with the results summary—sorry, little background noise —
[00:15] [Speaker 1]: um yeah that replay you ran, two runs, right? short and long.
[00:20] ElEna: yes, two replays. short one was our chat assistant typical traffic, median length ~18 tokens output; long one validated the 8k prefix caching and long prompts.
[00:28] Ravi: okay, great. so headline — across the short-head replay we measured ~2,200 tokens/sec per dollar on the s-run with continuous batching and 2ms median token. for the long run, tokens/sec per dollar dropped to ~820 given KV cache misses and long KV warmup. those are ballpark.
[00:45] Tom: can you repeat the tokens/sec per dollar numbers? 2,200 seems high. are we comparing the same model size?
[00:52] Ravi: good call — that's for the 7B quantized profile with xformers kernels. the long run used the 70B distill variant which naturally lowers tokens/sec per dollar. i should note we also changed the quantization from 4-bit dynamic to q8_0 for the long run which affects throughput.
[01:10] Elena: the big thing we saw was the prefix cache — when enabled on the 8k context prompts we got ~38% cost reduction overall on the long-run baseline, mostly because repeated system prompts cached. but cold-starts still hurt.
[01:25] Sanjay: about cold starts — does the runtime keep KV caches warm across lanes or is it per-inference? we've seen eviction when concurrency spikes.
[01:32] Ravi: currently the cache is per-session but we do continuous batching that merges KV where possible. eviction happens when memory pressure hits the GPU and the runtime respects LRU. we can tweak eviction thresholds in your pilot cluster — that was one of the config knobs we promised to test.
[01:45] [crosstalk]
[01:47] Ava: quick question — we're worried about tail latency. p95 spikes to 1.2s for some long prompts; what's the easy lever?
[01:55] Ravi: batching size and batch timeout are the quick wins. smaller max_batch and lower timeout reduces tail at cost of throughput. we also recommend enabling prefix caching aggressively for those long contexts — it reduces token generation time because prefix KV hits skip recompute.
[02:12] Jamie: could you show the batch vs latency trade-off numbers you ran?
[02:16] Ravi: yes — from last run: max_batch 32, timeout 20ms -> p95 1.2s, tokens/sec per dollar ~820. max_batch 8, timeout 5ms -> p95 540ms, tokens/sec per dollar ~1,100. so you buy latency.
[02:35] Tom: how stable are those numbers across time of day? i.e., if our traffic has diurnal peaks, will tokens/sec/$ drop further?
[02:43] Ravi: it can. with bursty peaks you see more cache churn and lower effective batching as requests miss windows. that's where dedicated capacity helps — reserved GPU lanes keep warm caches and predictable throughput.
[02:55] Elena: what's the rough delta in cost if we go dedicated for a month? ballpark.
[03:00] Jamie: we did a quick back-of-envelope: for your current replay scale, dedicated pool monthly commit is about 30% higher baseline but gives ~2.5x consistent tokens/sec in peak windows and reduces unpredictable tail. we'll follow up with exact numbers in the pricing addendum.
[03:20] Sanjay: security — we need to ensure keys don't leave our KMS. how does private deployment handle KMS integration?
[03:27] Ravi: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; hosted we do envelope encryption but keys can be customer-managed via cloud KMS. also audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. we'll include SOC2/ISO docs and the KMS flow diagram.
[03:40] Elena: thanks. also, on the caching savings — do you have an easy way to estimate savings if we increase prefix cache hit rate from 32% to 60%?
[03:48] Ravi: based on the model curves, roughly linear-ish for these patterns — increasing hit rate to 60% pushes long-run tokens/sec per dollar from ~820 to around ~1,100–1,250 depending on quant profile and kernel. i'll attach the calibration spreadsheet.
[04:05] [00:04:05] Marta: (note) attaching latency_heatmap_v2.png and tokens_per_dollar_calib.csv in chat.
[04:10] Elena: saw that — thanks.
[04:12] [00:04:12] Speaker 2: small transcription glitch here — some proper nouns got munged, e.g., xformers showing as ex-formers.
[04:18] Ravi: ha, expected. moving on — we also tested continuous batching with adaptive timeout which increases timeout during low load to batch more and decreases when latency jitter rises; that got us a middle ground: tokens/sec/$ ~1,050 with p95 ~700ms.
[04:34] Tom: interesting — what's the complexity to manage adaptive policy? do we need an operator?
[04:39] Ravi: we can run it out-of-the-box in pilot. SE will monitor and tune thresholds for two weeks; if you'd like we can push an autoscaling policy that ties batch timeout to p95 signals.
[04:50] Ava: product question — can we flag certain routes as latency-sensitive so they always get lower batching?
[04:55] Jamie: yes, per-route config is supported, you can set target latency SLO and cost-priorities per route. that will route requests through lower-batch queues or reserved lanes.
[05:06] Elena: about the per-route cost reporting — can we get token-level cost mapped to customer-facing features? we need that for internal chargeback.
[05:13] Marta: console has token-level breakdowns and you can tag routes; we'll share a short guide on tagging best-practices.
[05:19] Sanjay: one operational question — during the long-run we saw occasional evictions and a GPU OOM on one node. any idea why?
[05:26] Ravi: likely batch + prefill sizes exceeded available GPU when concurrent long contexts peaked. we recommend a soft cap on concurrent long-context sessions and to enable eviction thresholds earlier. also consider increasing worker count or using model parallel for the 70B variant.
[05:40] Tom: are there other quick quantization wins? we tried q4 and q8 and saw different tradeoffs.
[05:46] Ravi: yes, quantization is model- and workload-dependent. q4_0 gives better memory/cost but sometimes has minor quality regressions in generation; q8_0 is safer for quality but higher throughput cost. we can run signal-level evals — we did a small quality-check and saw negligible f1 drop for your prompts on q4_0 for the 7B, but larger models were less tolerant.
[06:05] Elena: how about hybrid approach — 7B q4 for most churn, 70B q8 for high-fidelity tasks?
[06:11] Jamie: that's a common pattern — route by intent. Redwood routing policy can fallback to a higher-fidelity variant on mismatch.
[06:18] [00:06:18] Speaker 3: minor noise — someone asked about competition.
[06:21] Tom: yeah, curious how you compare to Vertex and Anthropic on unit economics.
[06:25] Jamie: short answer: we optimize for production economics with caching and batching knobs; direct price per token might be similar but effective tokens/sec/$ can be better because of runtime caching and kernel optimizations. we'll include a competitive slide.
[06:36] Elena: on the pilot timeline — we're aiming to decide by mid-August if we scale. is that realistic?
[06:42] Jamie: yes, totally. if we deliver the replay results and the pricing addendum this week, and you run the 24h replay by Aug 5, decision mid-August is in reach.
[06:50] Ravi: last technical note — we found a subtle KV mismatch when prefix length > 6k in one run (some outputs truncated). i filed an internal bug ticket and patched the runtime for your cluster; we'll push the fix to the pilot cluster tonight.
[07:04] Elena: great, that might explain the truncations.
[07:07] Sanjay: will that patch require restarts?
[07:09] Ravi: small rolling restart, no full downtime. we'll schedule during your low-traffic window.
[07:15] Ava: question on monitoring — can we export per-token traces to our tracing system?
[07:20] Marta: yes, we have tracing hooks; per-token traces are heavy but you can sample. we'll share the tracer config.
[07:27] Tom: can we also get cost alerts when tokens/sec/$ dips below threshold?
[07:31] Jamie: yep, Console supports alerting on tokens-per-dollar and p95. we'll help set initial thresholds.
[07:38] [00:07:38] Ravi: quick recap of recommended config changes to test this week: 1) adaptive batching with timeout bounds 5–20ms; 2) increase prefix cache retention to reduce eviction; 3) soft cap concurrent long-context sessions; 4) run a 24-hr replay with both q4 and q8 profiles for the 7B and 70B variants.
[07:56] Elena: agreed. we'll run the replay and share logs.
[07:59] Jamie: next steps in chat — i'll send pricing addendum and the security pack.
[08:05] Tom: sounds good. any other risks?
[08:08] Ravi: only that cold-starts and cache churn can temporarily increase cost — mitigated by dedicated lanes or warming strategies.
[08:15] Ava: can you summarize the expected cost delta if we improve cache hit to 60%?
[08:18] Ravi: short answer — roughly +35–50% tokens/sec per dollar improvement on long runs, depending on model mix. details in spreadsheet.
[08:26] Marta: action items captured and i'll follow-up with a meeting note and links to the artifacts.
[08:31] Elena: thanks everyone — good sync.
[08:34] Jamie: thanks, we'll follow up. bye.

Meeting end.
